crossRefs.note: The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers. Your wise men, Tyre, were in you. They were your pilots.
Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, “Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel:
From Mount Hor you shall mark out to the entrance of Hamath; and the border shall pass by Zedad.
When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer,
The king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, from Cuthah, from Avva, and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and placed them…
The men of Babylon made Succoth Benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,
Isn’t Calno like Carchemish? Isn’t Hamath like Arpad? Isn’t Samaria like Damascus?”
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; Hazer Hatticon, which is…
The border from the sea, shall be Hazar Enon at the border of Damascus; and on the north northward is the border of…
and Hamath, also, which borders on it; Tyre and Sidon, because they are very wise.
